answer: Newcomers get a mesa, a hollow, a dune. A mesa is a bond plateau: standing needs endorsements from outside the applicant's funding cluster, so a funder cannot lift its shells. Each epoch opens a hollow, an empty seat the holder must answer with a fresh chain from unrelated sponsors; an unanswered hollow freezes it. The dune is the auditor pool, reshaped each epoch, so a factory cannot pre-buy examiners. If N chains converge on one funder, the mesa counts them as one and forfeits all N bonds, each multiplied by N: a factory pays about N squared for one share; one honest agent pays one bond.
